initial_labeled.note: Paper bootstraps with 20 uniformly-random labeled examples.
initial_labeled.unused_reason: This method bootstraps the labeled set via `construct_core_set(core_set_size)` (Stage 1 of the algorithm) — the initial labeled set IS the core-set. The spec's data_setup mentions `initial_labeled` for paradigm-fixed reasons but the algorithm's runtime path doesn't reference it. Kept in the dict for spec fidelity; ignore at runtime.

pool_size.reasoning: Paper uses the full training set (typically 60k–73k samples) as the unlabeled pool. We subsample to 800 to keep each round's gradient-embedding pass over the whole pool cheap (the pool is re-scored every round, so this is the dominant cost of the acquisition loop). Note: this is a smoke-scale default, not a runtime estimate — the smoke gate is what actually verifies the notebook fits its per-cell time budget. Pool ratio (total_budget / pool_size) ≈ 0.65. This exceeds the paradigm field guide's `demo_scale.max_budget_to_pool_ratio` of 0.4 — methods may converge before diversity is meaningfully tested. Increase pool_size (or reduce num_rounds × batch_size) for cleaner diversity-baseline comparisons.

learning_rate.reasoning: Paper does not explicitly specify the learning rate (spec.training.learning_rate: 'Paper does not explicitly state the optimizer or learning rate. The paper follows [5] (BatchBALD) which uses Adam with d'). Selected 0.001 based on Adam-default convention following standard deep AL practice (Gal et al. 2017, Kirsch et al. 2019).

max_epochs.reasoning: Paper trains until training accuracy ≥ 99% with no explicit epoch cap. At smoke scale the labeled sets are tiny (≤ ~500 examples) and `train_until_accuracy` usually stops well before the cap; 8 is a low safety bound that keeps per-round training fast at smoke scale. Increase it for full-scale training.

train_until_accuracy.note: Paper: train until training accuracy exceeds 99%.

hidden_dim.reasoning: Paper architecture choice is data-type-dependent. We use hidden_dim=256 as the field-guide-typical AL convention.

dropout_rate.reasoning: Bayesian-AL field guide recommends dropout in [0.25, 0.5] (Gal & Ghahramani 2016); 0.5 is the field-guide-typical default. Paper does not specify a dropout rate.

mc_samples.reasoning: Paper uses 2000 MC dropout samples. We use 20 — the bayesian-AL field-guide minimum for BALD's posterior estimate to be meaningful (Gal et al. recommend T ≥ 20). Larger T at paper scale gives a tighter estimate but dominates runtime at smoke scale.

core_set_size.reasoning: Paper states core_set_size=5000, but the generated method signature default is 100. Treating the signature default as the smoke/runtime value while preserving the paper value for audit.

R_0.reasoning: AUTO-RESOLVED (A001): the paper value is 2000.0, but this run uses 7.843. Derivation: 2000.0 * (1/255) = 7.843. The geometric prior p(y|x,theta) = R_0/||x-D_j|| uses raw L2 distances calibrated on MNIST's [0,255] pixel scale. Under ToTensor() normalization, pixel distances shrink by ~255×, so R_0 must shrink proportionally to preserve the same probability threshold the paper calibrated. This is a scale-dependent hyperparameter mismatch that breaks the algorithm's intended behavior. See assumptions.md entry A001. Previous note: Distance threshold for the geometric prior probability model p(y|x,theta) = 1 if ||x - Dj|| <= R_0 else R_0 / ||x - Dj||. The value 2000 is calibrated for raw [0, 255] pixel distances on MNIST. Under [0,1] normalization, distances scale by 1/255 and this threshold becomes ~7.8. Under [-1,1] preprocessing, it becomes ~15.6. The generator must not silently use the raw value with normalized data.

batch_returns.reasoning: Value from the pluggable_component signature default (batch_returns=300). The signature default is a runtime convenience chosen by the analyzer; it may or may not match the paper's stated value. If the paper specifies a value, add a structured source to the spec or make sure paper_map.json contains a clear batch_returns=<value> evidence entry so this value is resolved against paper-truth.
